title: Introducing Antioch: The Simulation Platform for Physical AI | Greylock
gist: Greylock is leading the Series A in Antioch, a startup building a hardware-calibrated, cloud-scale simulation platform meant to remove physical testing as the bottleneck for robots, drones, and autonomous systems; Amazon's Ring is already a customer.

insights.claim: Physical testing (equipment, facilities, engineering time) is the key bottleneck constraining how fast physical AI products (robots, drones, autonomous systems) can be developed and validated, especially for reproducing rare failure cases.
insights.speaker: Saam Motamedi
insights.so_what: Investors should look for infrastructure/tooling plays that attack physical-world validation costs, since that step -- not model capability -- is gating deployment speed.
insights.quote: Physical testing remains the key bottleneck.
insights.locator: Physical testing remains the key bottleneck.

insights.claim: As foundation models become more capable, the speed at which teams can validate those capabilities in the physical world will increasingly determine how fast products reach market -- validation speed, not model quality alone, becomes the differentiator.
insights.speaker: Saam Motamedi
insights.so_what: Signals a coming shift in competitive advantage from model capability to simulation/validation infrastructure -- watch for consolidation around simulation platforms as a chokepoint.
insights.quote: As models become more capable, the speed of validation will increasingly determine how quickly teams can bring products to market.
insights.locator: Physical testing remains the key bottleneck.

insights.claim: Just as AI transformed how fast software teams could build products, a similar transformation is expected for physical AI (robots, drones, autonomous systems), implying a coming acceleration in hardware-embodied AI development cycles.
insights.speaker: Saam Motamedi
insights.so_what: Frames physical AI as following the software-speed trajectory of the LLM era, a thesis that could justify premium valuations for infra startups serving this transition.
insights.quote: AI has transformed how quickly software teams can build products. Physical AI is poised for a similar transformation.
insights.locator: AI has transformed how quickly software teams can build products.

insights.claim: Antioch's platform calibrates high-fidelity simulations to a customer's specific hardware using real-world data, then runs those simulations at cloud scale, letting teams move from a single physical experiment to thousands of parallel evaluations to identify weaknesses and validate improvements before deployment.
insights.speaker: Saam Motamedi
insights.so_what: The core product mechanism (hardware-calibrated sim + cloud-scale parallel evaluation) is the moat to evaluate against competitors -- check whether rivals can match the real-world calibration step, not just raw simulation throughput.
insights.quote: Its platform calibrates high-fidelity simulations to customers’ hardware using real-world data, then runs them at cloud scale.
insights.locator: Antioch brings the speed of software development to physical AI.

insights.claim: Antioch is already working with leading physical AI teams, including Amazon's Ring, which have used the platform to accelerate the speed at which they develop and bring products to market.
insights.speaker: Saam Motamedi
insights.so_what: Amazon Ring as a named reference customer at Series A stage is a strong early commercial validation signal, unusually concrete for a seed/Series A announcement -- worth tracking whether other large hardware/IoT players follow.
insights.quote: Antioch is already working with leading physical AI teams, including Amazon’s Ring, which have accelerated the speed at which they can develop and bring products to market.
insights.locator: Antioch brings the speed of software development to physical AI.

insights.claim: Antioch's founders Harry Mellsop, Alex Langshur, and Michael Calvey previously built Transpose together, which was acquired by Chainalysis, giving the team prior company-building and successful-exit experience before starting Antioch.
insights.speaker: Saam Motamedi
insights.so_what: A repeat-founder team with a prior acquisition (by Chainalysis) de-risks execution for Series A investors evaluating team quality.
insights.quote: Harry Mellsop, Alex Langshur, and Michael Calvey previously built Transpose together, which was acquired by Chainalysis.
insights.locator: The Antioch founding team combines company-building experience

insights.claim: Antioch's technical bench includes Harry Mellsop's prior computer vision work at Tesla and Collin Schlager's experience in simulation, machine learning, and hardware from Meta Reality Labs, combining deep domain expertise in both perception and simulation.
insights.speaker: Saam Motamedi
insights.so_what: Big-tech pedigree in the exact adjacent domains (autonomy CV at Tesla, simulation/hardware at Meta Reality Labs) suggests the team can credibly build hardware-calibrated simulation infrastructure, a technically hard problem.
insights.quote: Harry also worked on computer vision at Tesla, while Collin Schlager brings experience in simulation, machine learning, and hardware from Meta Reality Labs.
insights.locator: The Antioch founding team combines company-building experience

insights.claim: Greylock is leading the Series A funding round in Antioch, positioning the firm early in the physical AI simulation/validation infrastructure category.
insights.speaker: Saam Motamedi
insights.so_what: Marks a concrete VC entry point and price-setting event in the physical AI simulation sub-sector -- useful for benchmarking later rounds or competitor valuations.
insights.quote: Greylock is leading the Series A in Antioch, a company building the simulation platform for physical AI.

insights.claim: Greylock's stated thesis is that the companies able to turn advances in AI into reliable, deployed products -- not just capable models -- will help define the next generation of industry, and it views Antioch's simulation platform as core infrastructure for that transition.
insights.speaker: Saam Motamedi
insights.so_what: Signals where a major VC is directing capital within AI: toward reliability/deployment infrastructure rather than model-layer bets, a useful positioning cue for allocators tracking AI infra sub-themes.
insights.quote: We believe the companies that turn advances in AI into reliable products will help define the next generation of industry.
